title: Battle of Maysalun: French defeat Syrian forces
why: French victory ends Faisal's Syrian kingdom and opens the way to the Mandate over Syria and Lebanon.

title: League of Nations confirms French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon
why: The mandate's legal basis: Lebanon's pre-independence status and its later constitution rest on this document.

title: Charles Debbas becomes first president of the Lebanese Republic
why: First head of state under the new constitution, chosen by parliament under French supervision.

title: France suspends Lebanese constitution at outbreak of World War II
why: Mandate authorities dissolve parliament and rule by decree, fuelling the independence drive that follows. (corrected from 1939-09-21) [corrected from 1939-09-21: source gives September 1939, day not stated; one source says July 1939 dissolution]

title: Allies invade Syria and Lebanon against Vichy France
why: Operation Exporter: British, Australian and Free French forces take Lebanon, paving the way for independence.

title: Lebanon co-founds the Arab League in Cairo
why: Lebanon's Arab alignment and the 'Arab face' formula of the National Pact are embedded in the League charter.

title: French bombardment of Damascus; Levant crisis
why: Crisis pushes Britain to intervene and forces France's exit from Syria and Lebanon in 1946.

title: Israel declared; first wave of Palestinian refugees enters Lebanon
why: The 1948 exodus puts roughly 100,000 Palestinians in Lebanon; their status stays unresolved today.

title: UN General Assembly creates UNRWA
why: UNRWA becomes the agency for Palestinian refugees in Lebanon's camps, including schools and health services.

title: President Bechara el-Khoury resigns after general strike
why: Opposition 'white revolution' forces him out; Chamoun is elected five days later.

title: Chamoun accepts the Eisenhower Doctrine
why: Alignment with the West splits Lebanon between Nasserist and pro-Western camps and leads to the 1958 revolt.

title: Parliamentary elections under Chehab
why: Chehab-era elections under a 99-seat system; first polls after the 1958 crisis.

title: Parliamentary elections: Tripartite Alliance wins
why: Chehabists lose to the Maronite Tripartite Alliance, a step towards the 1970 presidential vote.

title: PM Rashid Karami resigns after clashes over Palestinian guerrillas
why: Government vacuum of about six months ends only with the Cairo Agreement in November.

title: Jordan expels PLO; fedayeen relocate to Lebanon
why: Lebanon becomes the PLO's main base, deepening the pressure that erupts in 1975.

title: Last parliamentary elections before the civil war
why: The 1972 parliament stays in place until 1992 because elections were postponed through the war. (corrected from 1972-04-09)

title: Yom Kippur War; Lebanese front limited
why: Lebanon stays largely out, but Palestinian and Israeli operations along the border intensify afterwards.

title: Musa al-Sadr launches Movement of the Deprived in Baalbek
why: Mobilises Lebanon's Shia community; its militia wing Amal is formed in 1975.

title: Noureddine Rifai's military cabinet resigns
why: Short-lived military cabinet falls in the first weeks of the war; Rashid Karami takes over on 1 July. (corrected from 1975-05-23) [corrected from 1975-05-23: military government formed 23 May, resigned 26 May 1975]

title: Amal militia announced by Musa al-Sadr
why: Amal becomes the main Shia militia and later the Berri-led party, a pillar of the post-war system.

title: Battle of the Hotels begins in downtown Beirut
why: Fighting over the hotel district destroys central Beirut and divides the city.

title: US ambassador Francis Meloy killed in Beirut
why: Kidnapped and murdered at a checkpoint; US evacuates Americans by sea days later.

title: Siege of Tel al-Zaatar camp begins
why: Christian militias besiege the Palestinian camp in east Beirut until its fall on 12 August.

title: Salim al-Hoss forms technocratic cabinet
why: Sarkis-era cabinet of non-politicians during the first ceasefire period.

title: Coastal Road massacre by Fatah commandos
why: Attack near Tel Aviv kills Israelis and triggers Israel's Litani operation three days later.

title: Ali Hassan Salameh killed by Mossad car bomb in Beirut
why: Fatah security chief linked to Munich 1972 killed in Beirut.

title: Iranian Revolution triumphs
why: Sets the stage for Iranian revolutionaries to form Hezbollah in Lebanon after 1982.

title: Egypt-Israel peace treaty signed in Washington
why: Isolates Egypt from the Arab world; Lebanon remains the active front line with Israel.

title: Iraq invades Iran, starting eight-year war
why: Iran-Iraq war diverts Tehran's attention but builds the Revolutionary Guards and their Lebanese outreach.

title: Shafik Wazzan forms cabinet
why: Wazzan cabinet governs through the 1982 invasion and the Amine Gemayel handover.

title: Israel annexes the Golan Heights
why: Annexation keeps Syria-Israel tension alive and feeds Shebaa Farms disputes after 2000.

title: Hama massacre in Syria
why: Assad crushes the Muslim Brotherhood; Syria's later Lebanon policy hardens against Islamist and Palestinian rivals.

title: Hezbollah emerges in Bekaa with Iranian Revolutionary Guards
why: Iranian guard units in Baalbek train Shia militants; Hezbollah's formation dates to this summer.

title: Israeli ambassador Shlomo Argov shot in London
why: Abu Nidal gunmen; Israel uses it as pretext for the invasion of Lebanon three days later.

title: Israeli forces take Beaufort Castle
why: Fall of the PLO stronghold opens the road to Beirut.

title: Battle of Sultan Yacoub: Syria and Israel clash
why: Syrian and Israeli armour fight in the Bekaa; Syria loses air defences in the following days.

title: Multinational Force deploys to Beirut
why: US, French and Italian troops arrive to supervise the PLO exit; they return after Sabra and Shatila.

title: Yasser Arafat leaves Beirut
why: PLO leadership relocates to Tunis, ending its decade-long Lebanese base.

title: Tyre: Israeli military HQ destroyed by car bomb
why: One of the first major suicide attacks in Lebanon; linked later to Hezbollah's founding milieu.

title: Battle of Souk El Gharb; US Navy shells the Chouf
why: US naval gunfire supports the army; a turning point that makes the MNF a party to the fighting.

title: Suicide truck bomb hits Israeli HQ in Tyre again
why: Second Tyre bombing kills dozens and accelerates the Israeli exit from Lebanon. (WaPo, 5 Nov 1983, gives at least 39 dead for the bombing; Wikipedia gives 28 Israelis and 32 Lebanese)

title: Kuwait embassy bombings link Lebanese Shia network
why: Bombings tied to Lebanese and Iraqi Shia militants; the jailed 'Kuwait 17' become a motive for Beirut hostage-taking.

title: Arafat leaves Tripoli after Syrian-backed siege
why: Last PLO exit from Lebanon's north; Syria consolidates its role.

title: AUB president Malcolm Kerr assassinated
why: Shot on the AUB campus; early sign of the hostage-and-murder campaign against Westerners.

title: Rashid Karami forms national unity government
why: A six-man cabinet of main militia leaders, aiming to end the war and cancel the 17 May Agreement.

title: Bir al-Abed bombing targets Sheikh Fadlallah
why: A car bomb kills scores outside a Shia mosque in Beirut's south; the target survives.

title: Elie Hobeika ousted as Lebanese Forces leader
why: Geagea's coup dismantles the Tripartite Agreement's Christian partner.

title: Terry Waite kidnapped in Beirut
why: Envoy of the Archbishop of Canterbury held until 1991; emblem of the Western hostage crisis.

title: Grand Mufti Hassan Khaled assassinated
why: Car bomb kills the Sunni religious leader; Taif talks continue amid sectarian tension.

title: Elias Hrawi elected president
why: Elected in Shtoura after Moawad's assassination; Hrawi's term later extended twice.

title: Iraq invades Kuwait; Gulf crisis opens
why: US needs Syria's support against Saddam; Damascus's hand in Lebanon is freed and the 13 Oct assault follows.

title: Omar Karami forms first post-war government
why: The first cabinet under Taif and Syrian tutelage; ends in May 1992 after riots.

title: Lebanese army fights PLO at Sidon and Ain al-Hilweh
why: Army drives Palestinian factions from Sidon's environs, completing state control except in the camps.

title: Madrid Peace Conference opens
why: Lebanon takes part in bilateral talks with Israel; Syria links its track to Lebanon's.

title: Omar Karami government resigns after cost-of-living protests
why: Riots over the collapsing pound topple the cabinet and lead to the 1992 elections and Hariri.

title: Oslo Accords signed in Washington
why: Hezbollah and Damascus oppose it; the 13 Sept Dahieh protest follows and Lebanon-Israel track remains frozen.

title: Parliamentary elections, Hariri list wins Beirut
why: Second post-war elections under Syrian oversight with boycotts from Christian leaders.

title: Pope John Paul II visits Lebanon
why: Signs the Apostolic Exhortation 'A New Hope for Lebanon' for the post-synod; first papal visit. [visit was 10-11 May 1997; exhortation signed 10 May at Harissa]

title: Salim al-Hoss forms government under Lahoud
why: Hoss government of technocrats begins an austerity drive against Hariri's policies.

title: Hafez al-Assad dies; Bashar inherits power
why: Syria's dominance in Lebanon continues; the transition is followed by calls for Syrian withdrawal.

title: UN certifies Israeli withdrawal; Blue Line drawn
why: UN says Israel complied with UNSCR 425; Lebanon disputes Shebaa Farms, and Hezbollah keeps arms.

title: Hezbollah captures three Israeli soldiers at Shebaa Farms
why: Capture leads to the 2004 prisoner swap; underscores the Shebaa issue.

title: Syria redeploys troops out of Beirut
why: Partial pullback to the Bekaa after domestic pressure; first concession before 2005.

title: Elie Hobeika killed by car bomb in Beirut
why: Former militia chief who was to testify on Sabra and Shatila in Belgium is assassinated.

title: Arab summit in Beirut adopts Arab Peace Initiative
why: Beirut summit's initiative offers normalisation in return for Israeli withdrawal and a Palestinian state.

title: US-led invasion of Iraq begins
why: Reshapes regional balance; Washington turns toward Syria's role, leading to UNSCR 1559 in 2004.

title: Rafic Hariri resigns as prime minister
why: Quits weeks after the Lahoud extension; he is assassinated four months later.

title: Omar Karami resigns as government after Cedar protests
why: Pro-Syrian cabinet falls after two weeks of protests; he is reappointed then resigns again.

title: Najib Mikati forms caretaker cabinet to run elections
why: Interim government delivers the 2005 elections.

title: 2005 parliamentary elections finish; March 14 wins
why: First vote after Syrian withdrawal; Saad Hariri's bloc wins majority.

title: Fouad Siniora forms first post-Syria government
why: Hezbollah and Amal ministers join a government for the first time.

title: Four pro-Syrian generals arrested in Hariri probe
why: Jamil al-Sayyed, Ali al-Hajj, Raymond Azar, Mustafa Hamdan detained on UN investigator's request.

title: Mehlis report implicates Syrian and Lebanese officials
why: UN investigator's interim report sharpens the Syria crisis and leads to the STL.

title: National Dialogue opens at parliament
why: Leaders discuss Hezbollah's arms, Palestinian weapons and Shebaa; talks stall before July war.

title: Israeli air strike on Qana kills civilians
why: Air strike on a building in Qana, killing dozens of civilians, brings calls for a ceasefire.

title: UN Security Council adopts Resolution 1701
why: Ends the July war, calls for Hezbollah disarmament south of Litani and expands UNIFIL.

title: Six UNIFIL peacekeepers killed in Khiam bombing
why: Spanish peacekeepers die when a roadside bomb hits their vehicle.

title: Hezbollah commander Imad Mughniyeh killed in Damascus
why: Car bomb kills the operations chief of Hezbollah, blamed on Israel.

title: National unity cabinet formed after Doha Agreement
why: Siniora cabinet gives opposition a blocking third.

title: Hezbollah-Israel prisoner exchange: Samir Kuntar freed
why: Bodies of two Israeli soldiers for Kuntar and four Hezbollah fighters.

title: Lebanon and Syria establish diplomatic relations
why: First formal ties in history; embassies opened after decades of Syrian denial.

title: Saad Hariri forms national unity government
why: Ends five-month stalemate after June 2009 elections.

title: Parliament eases Palestinian labour and social security rights
why: Amendments open some jobs to registered Palestinian refugees but leave property-ownership ban.

title: Syrian uprising begins in Daraa
why: Protests turn into civil war; spills into Lebanon via refugees, Tripoli clashes and Hezbollah's entry.

title: Najib Mikati forms Hezbollah-backed government
why: Formed after five months of vacuum; survives until March 2013.

title: Pope Benedict XVI visits Lebanon
why: Signs post-synodal exhortation for Middle East Christians amid Syrian war. [visit was 14-16 Sep 2012; exhortation signed 14 Sep at Harissa]

title: Mikati resigns
why: Citing deadlock over election law and the security chiefs' terms; 10 months for Salam.

title: Battle of Qusayr: Hezbollah enters Syrian war
why: Hezbollah fighters help Syrian army retake Qusayr near the Lebanese border.

title: Israeli strike in Quneitra kills Hezbollah commanders and IRGC general
why: Jihad Mughniyeh and Iranian general killed; Hezbollah retaliates at Shebaa 10 days later.

title: Saad Hariri forms government under Aoun
why: Government formed six weeks after Aoun's election; holds the 2018 polls.

title: Hariri returns to Beirut, rescinds Riyadh resignation in Dec
why: Ends an 18-day crisis with Saudi Arabia after French mediation.

title: Hassan Diab government wins confidence vote
why: Government backed by Hezbollah; falls after the port blast.

title: Macron visits Beirut after port explosion
why: First foreign leader in the ruins; promises a new political pact and hosts donors on 9 August.

title: Macron returns; roadmap for reform demanded
why: Second visit on Lebanon's centenary; pushes the Adib government and a reform timetable.

title: Abraham Accords: UAE and Bahrain normalise with Israel
why: Gulf normalisation reshapes Arab positions and Lebanon's Arab Peace Initiative stance.

title: Mustapha Adib gives up forming a government
why: Macron initiative stalls over the finance ministry dispute.

title: Saad Hariri designated PM again; fails
why: Designated for a fourth time; cannot form cabinet with Aoun and resigns the mandate in July 2021.

title: Activist Lokman Slim found shot dead
why: Publisher and Hezbollah critic killed in the south; case unsolved.

title: Hariri gives up forming a government
why: Ends nine months of failed formation; Mikati is named on 26 July.

title: Saudi Arabia expels Lebanese ambassador over Kordahi remarks
why: Gulf-Lebanon diplomatic crisis; Saudi ban on Lebanese imports follows. (corrected from 2021-10-30)

title: Nabih Berri re-elected parliament speaker
why: Seventh term for the speaker despite loss of the Hezbollah-allied majority. [Wikipedia confirms 2022 re-election as seventh term but gives no reliable day; 31 May 2022 date unverified]

title: Irish peacekeeper Seán Rooney killed in Al-Aqbiyah
why: UNIFIL soldier shot dead when peacekeepers' vehicles were attacked; a Hezbollah-linked suspect was later tried.

title: Twelfth presidential vote fails: Azour vs Frangieh
why: Parliament splits; no candidate reaches the two-thirds quorum.

title: Ain al-Hilweh clashes: Fatah and Islamist groups
why: Week of clashes in Lebanon's largest camp kills about a dozen and displaces thousands.

title: Hamas attack on Israel; Gaza war begins
why: Triggers Hezbollah's front on 8 October and the 2024 Lebanon war.

title: Hamas deputy leader Saleh al-Arouri killed in Dahieh
why: First Israeli strike on Beirut's southern suburbs since 2006.

title: Iran launches missiles and drones at Israel
why: First direct Iranian attack; raises stakes in the Lebanon front.

title: Rocket strike on Majdal Shams kills 12 children and youths
why: Israel blames Hezbollah, which denies it; Israel retaliates with Shukr's killing three days later.

title: Hezbollah commander Fuad Shukr killed in Dahieh
why: Israel says he ordered Majdal Shams strike; killing followed by Haniyeh's in Tehran.

title: Hezbollah and Israel exchange large strikes after Shukr's killing
why: Israel strikes first; Hezbollah launches rockets and drones in its announced retaliation.

title: Radwan Force commander Ibrahim Aqil killed in Beirut
why: Israeli strike kills Aqil and other commanders in Dahieh.

title: Israel launches mass air campaign on Lebanon
why: Strikes kill hundreds in a day, the deadliest since 2006; leads to ground invasion on 1 October.

title: Iran fires ballistic missiles at Israel
why: Second direct Iranian attack, launched as Israel invades south Lebanon and after Nasrallah's killing.

title: Israeli fire hits UNIFIL positions in Naqoura
why: Peacekeepers injured; troop-contributing countries protest.

title: Hezbollah confirms Hashem Safieddine killed in Israeli strike
why: Nasrallah's presumed successor killed in early October strike on Dahieh; Naim Qassem succeeds on 29 October.

title: Israeli fire kills 22 Lebanese returning to border villages
why: Day before the ceasefire's 60-day withdrawal deadline, residents approaching villages are shot; 124 wounded.

title: Israel strikes Dahieh for first time since the 2024 ceasefire
why: Strike on Beirut's southern suburbs after rockets fired from Lebanon; Lebanon denies involvement.

title: Mahmoud Abbas visits Beirut; camp disarmament agreed
why: Lebanon and PA agree to start disarming Palestinian camps. [page confirms May 2025 Aoun-Abbas meeting; exact day 21 May not stated]

title: Israel strikes Iran; twelve-day war begins
why: Israel-Iran war; Hezbollah stays out, signalling its weakened state.

title: Fatah begins handing over weapons in Burj el-Barajneh
why: First camp arms handover under the state's monopoly-on-arms plan. [page confirms camp weapons handovers began August 2025; Fatah at Burj el-Barajneh on 21 Aug not stated]

title: Israeli defence minister says Israel will occupy up to the Litani
why: Katz announces demolition of border villages and a lasting presence south of the Litani; Lebanon calls it an occupation plan.

title: Israeli shelling kills Indonesian UNIFIL peacekeeper at Aadchit al-Qusayr
why: First UNIFIL death of the 2026 war, followed the next day by two more Indonesian deaths.

title: Explosion kills two more Indonesian UNIFIL peacekeepers
why: Convoy vehicle hit by an explosion; UNIFIL casualties add pressure ahead of its scheduled 2026 closure.

title: Israeli strike in Beirut kills Hezbollah Southern Front commander
why: Hajj Yusuf Ismail Hashem killed; his predecessor Ali Karaki died in September 2024.

title: Israel orders evacuation of Beirut's southern suburbs
why: Evacuation order for Dahieh ahead of strikes on what the IDF calls Hezbollah infrastructure.

title: French UNIFIL soldier killed in Ghandourieh attack
why: French peacekeeper dies after an attack on UNIFIL; responsibility disputed between parties.

title: Lebanese army withdraws from Kfar Tibnit
why: Army pulls out as Israeli troops operate around Nabatieh.

title: Battle for Ali al-Taher hill near Nabatieh
why: Israeli attempt to take a ridge southeast of Nabatieh; Hezbollah says it repelled offensives; fighting continues into August.

title: Iran says US, Iran and Lebanon agree committee to oversee war's end
why: Announcement by Tehran of a committee; Lebanese government statements on it differ.

title: Netanyahu says Israel will keep occupying south Lebanon
why: Israel says it will maintain the buffer zone; Lebanon rejects annexation claims by some villages.

title: Israeli forces advance beyond Yellow Line into Haris
why: Advance past the US-brokered line, with demolitions in Khiam, Taybeh, Mays al-Jabal and Yohmor.
